description:
Looking for motivated and creative people to join our team for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 – Planet X and SPHEREx! 

Interested in programming, astronomy, data analysis, or design? Let's work together to explore infrared images, uncover hidden objects, and build something amazing! 🚀
summary:
Stella Astro Viewer is a browser-based infrared astronomical workbench built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to make raw multi-mission telescope data accessible without heavy desktop software. Instead of forcing users to download massive FITS archives or write custom scripts, Stella pulls calibrated cutouts directly from NASA’s WISE/NEOWISE, 2MASS, and SPHEREx spectral architectures alongside ESA Gaia DR3 and SIMBAD catalogs.

Inside a single responsive workspace, researchers and citizen scientists can blend infrared wavelength bands into false-color composites, inspect 102-band spectral curves for water-ice and methane signatures, and animate 14 years of archival frames (2010–2024) to spot fast-moving cosmic neighbors like the nearby Y-type brown dwarf WISE 0855−0714. Built with Next.js, TypeScript, and custom HTML5 Canvas FITS rendering, Stella includes sigma-clipped noise reduction, quadrature motion subtraction, and resilient server-side caching so deep-sky exploration stays fast and scientifically reliable right in the browser.
details:
What It Does & How It Works Stella Astro Viewer is a browser-based, multi-mission infrared astronomical workbench designed around NASA’s SPHEREx 6-array spectral architecture ($0.75\text{–}5.0\ \mu\text{m}$). When a user searches any sky coordinate or selects a benchmark target, Stella queries NASA/IPAC IRSA archives (WISE/NEOWISE and 2MASS), CDS HiPS2FITS (DSS2 Optical), and ESA Gaia DR3 / SIMBAD catalogs, aligns the cutouts onto a common World Coordinate System (WCS) grid, and renders raw 32-bit FITS data directly in the browser via HTML5 Canvas. Users can blend infrared bands into false-color composites, inspect a live 102-band spectral curve ($0.75\text{–}5.0\ \mu\text{m}$) with CSV export, and animate 14 years of archival epochs (2010–2024) using a quadrature-gated $\vert{}B - A\vert{}$ difference blinker to isolate fast-moving celestial objects.

Benefits & Intended Impact Professional infrared FITS analysis traditionally requires installing heavy desktop tools (such as SAOImageDS9) or writing custom Python/Astropy pipelines. Stella lowers that barrier to a single web link, empowering students, educators, and citizen scientists (such as Backyard Worlds volunteers) to visually explore deep-sky dust structures, identify chemical absorption dips like water ice ($3.0\ \mu\text{m}$) and methane ($3.3\ \mu\text{m}$), and spot high-proper-motion brown dwarfs and nearby stars in real time.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend & Rendering: Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, HTML5 <canvas> 32-bit FITS renderer, and Recharts.
  • Backend & Caching: Next.js serverless API routes with request deduplication and persistent disk caching (/tmp on Vercel / .cache/irsa locally).
  • Astronomical Archives & Protocols: NASA/IPAC IRSA Image Server (IBE) & SIA v2, CDS HiPS2FITS, ESA Gaia DR3, and CDS SIMBAD TAP.
  • Deployment & Dev Environment: Vercel CI/CD, GitHub, Arch Linux (Hyprland/Neovim), and Windows.

Creativity & Design Approach Rather than building a static image gallery, we treated the browser like a real observatory instrument—combining a 100vh zero-scroll scientific cockpit layout with Lupton asinh HDR stretching, live WCS cursor telemetry, dynamic angular scale bars, and an extensible + Add Source registry that lets researchers plug in new HiPS2FITS, IRSA SIA v2, or direct FITS endpoints without touching code.

Key Factors & Engineering Considerations

  • Scientific Rigor (Same-Instrument Subtraction): To prevent false difference rings caused by differing telescope pixel scales ($1.0''$ 2MASS vs. $2.75''$ WISE) and point-spread functions, pixel-by-pixel $\vert{}B - A\vert{}$ subtraction is strictly constrained to same-instrument epochs, while cross-survey comparisons use safe visual blinking.
  • Noise & Artifact Suppression: Raw infrared cutouts suffer from hot pixels, cosmic rays, and subtraction banding; we implemented 3-iteration sigma-clipped sky floors, $3\times3$ median despckling, and quadrature noise gating ($3.5\sqrt{\sigma_A^2 + \sigma_B^2}$).
  • Network Resilience & Provenance Transparency: To handle intermittent upstream archive timeouts (HTTP 502/404), we built retry logic, INTERSECT=OVERLAPS queries, server-side caching, and clear UI badges distinguishing direct archival FITS pixels from hybrid spectral models.
